Its cyclotomic character factors through $\Gamma=\mathcal M/\mathcal G$ and has open image in $\widehat\Z^\times$. We do not require $\widehat{\mathcal G_0}\cong\mathcal G$, which the manuscript expressly does not require at scan206. A Lie approximation is an affine finite-type $\Q$-group $G$, a character $\chi_G:G\to\Gm$, and a continuous homomorphism $\rho:\mathcal M\to G(\mathbb A_f)$ such that \[ \chi_G\rho=\chi,\qquad \rho(\mathcal G_0)\subset G(\Q), \] where $\Q$ is embedded diagonally, and such that no proper closed $\Q$-subgroup contains $\rho(\mathcal M)$ adelically. These are conditions $1^\circ,2^\circ,3^\circ$ forte, and $4^\circ$ of scans202--208.

statement: Two explicitly chosen Malcev stages — For types $(0,3),(0,4),(1,1)$ the geometric discrete group is free of rank $r=2,3,2$. Choose rational Malcev nilpotence-class truncation. Its first stages are \[ U_1=\Ga^r,\qquad U_2=\bigl(V\oplus\Lambda^2V,*\bigr),\qquad (v,a)*(w,b)=(v+w,a+b+\tfrac12v\wedge w). \] The Lie bracket is $[v,w]=v\wedge w$ and $\Lambda^2V$ is central; lower-central degrees are $1,2$. For punctured spheres the graded Galois representations are $\Q_\ell(1)^r$ and $\Q_\ell(2)^{\binom r2}$; for a punctured elliptic curve they are $T_\ell E\otimes\Q_\ell$ and $\Q_\ell(1)$. Permutations of punctures act on $V$ by permuting peripheral classes subject to their sum being zero, and act by the exterior square in degree two.

statement: Typed comparisons for finite quotients — Let $F=F_2$, $F\twoheadrightarrow H$, $d=|H|$, and $N$ its kernel. The prompt's comparison map exists only when this finite quotient factors through the chosen approximation. In that case it is surjective, with the following images and kernels: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{approximation}&\text{image}&\text{kernel}\\ \hline (-)^{\ab}&N/F'&(N\cap F')/N'\\ (-)/(-)''&N/F''&F''/N''\\ (-)/\gamma_{c+1}&N/\gamma_{c+1}F& \gamma_{c+1}F/\gamma_{c+1}N . \end{array} \] The required conditions are respectively $H$ abelian, $H''=1$, and $\gamma_{c+1}H=1$. The first kernel is free abelian of rank $d-1$. None of these three maps is an isomorphism for $d>1$. Pro-$\ell$ completion is exact for all finite $\ell$-group quotients; other finite groups cannot be its continuous quotients. A connected prounipotent $\Q$-group has no nontrivial finite étale quotient.

statement: The Fermat cover and relative completion — For $N=\ker(F_2\to(\Z/n)^2)$, $n>1$, the absolute map $N^{\un}_\Q\to (F_2^{\un})_\Q$ is surjective. statement: Exact modules and the three tripod dimension sequences — Let $L(V)$ be the free Lie algebra over $\Z$, with $V=\Z^q/\Z(1,\ldots,1)$, $r=q-1$, and let $\mathfrak s_{r,n}$ denote degree-$n$ tangential special derivations modulo inner derivations. For $n\ge2$ there is an $S_q$-equivariant exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\mathfrak s_{r,n} \longrightarrow V\otimes L_n(V) \xrightarrow{[\, ,\, ]}L_{n+1}(V)\longrightarrow0. \] In degree one one additionally divides by the $q$ peripheral centralizer lines. Consequently \[ \dim\mathfrak s_{r,n}=r\ell_n(r)-\ell_{n+1}(r) -(r+1)\delta_{n,1}, \qquad \ell_n(r)=\frac1n\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)r^{n/d}. \] For the tripod, the dimensions through weight fourteen are: \input{sections/B_tripod_table.tex} Here raw cycles means $\psi(x,y)+\psi(y,x)=0$ and $\psi(x,y)+\psi(y,z)+\psi(z,x)=0$, $z=-x-y$. The special-invariant column instead imposes antisymmetry and \[ J(\psi)=[x,\psi(x,y)]-[x+y,\psi(-x-y,y)]=0. \] The last column is the free graded Lie algebra on one generator in each odd degree at least three; no equality with all of $\grt_1$ is built into this computation.

statement: The integral envelope of each virtually abelian stage — Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely generated group with a normal lattice $M\cong\Z^r$ of finite index. For $n\ge1$ form the group scheme $\Gamma_{nM}$ whose components are indexed by $\Gamma/nM$ and whose identity component is $(nM)\otimes\Ga$. Put \[ E_\Gamma=\varprojlim_{n\mid n'}\Gamma_{nM}. \] For every ring $A$ and every closed finitely presented subgroup $G\subset\GL_{d,A}$, restriction to the canonical homomorphism $\Gamma\to E_\Gamma(A)$ induces a bijection \[ \Hom_{A\text{-groups}}((E_\Gamma)_A,G) \ \cong\ \{\rho:\Gamma\to G(A):\rho(\gamma) \text{ is fibrewise quasi-unipotent for all }\gamma\in\Gamma\}. \] The construction is independent of $M$ up to the unique isomorphism compatible with $\Gamma$. This is the functorial, direct-limit reading of \MS{50}{663--663'}{31--32}, rather than an inverse limit of Hom sets.

statement: Filling and the virtually abelian system — Let $F=F_r$ and let $q:F\twoheadrightarrow F_{r-1}$ kill one chosen free generator, with kernel $R$. statement: Precise comparisons with weighted and Teichm\"uller completions — There is a natural morphism from the pro-object $\mathscr E$ of B.2 to the image closure of every compatible adelic finite-jet representation furnished by $\GT$ or $\GT_{\rm ell}$. There is no unconditional identification of these targets with $\mathscr E$. Its weighted completion $\mathcal W_{\rho_\ell,w}$ maps uniquely to a finite-type target $H_\ell$ over $R$ whenever the representation into $H_\ell(\Q_\ell)$ lifts $\rho_\ell$ and $\ker(H_\ell\to R)$ is unipotent with strictly negative $w$-weights on its abelianization. For targets defined over $\Q$ with the compatible adelic representation of B.1, the comparison diagram is \[ \mathscr E_{\Q_\ell}\longrightarrow (H_{\mathbb A})_{\Q_\ell} \longleftarrow\mathcal W_{\rho_\ell,w}, \] where $H_{\mathbb A}$ is the $\Q$-Zariski closure of the adelic image. The right arrow has image the $\Q_\ell$-Zariski closure of the $\ell$-adic image; these two closures need not be equal.
